chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
Any woman and any fearful man who departs from al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām at night, there is no harm in that; so let him cast the pebble at the Jamrah. And he mentioned the hadith to its end.

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: departed or moved on ritually from a sacred station
key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: the Jamrah, the stoning site in the hajj ritual
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: the sacred site of al-Muzdalifah during hajj rites
key_terms.خَائِفٍ: a person in a state of fear, for whom the concession applies
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permitted

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for women or fearful men to depart from al-Muzdalifah before dawn and stone the Jamrah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal concession regarding departing from al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām during the night before dawn. It indicates that for a woman and for a man who is afraid, there is no harm in leaving early and proceeding with the rite of stoning the Jamrah.
